stem: A policy has the greatest expected return, but one noisy episode gives a poor reward. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: A poor realization alone does not refute optimality in expected return.
An optimal policy must maximize every possible realized trajectory simultaneously.
The single poor episode establishes a lower expected return than a competitor whose only observed episode was better.
Maximizing expected return also establishes that the policy minimizes outcome variance.

stem: For FetchReachDense-v4 in the explicitly checked Gymnasium 1.4.0/Gymnasium-Robotics 1.4.2 setup with its default 50-step wrapper, which statement correctly qualifies the lecture’s termination wording?

options.text: terminated and truncated are aliases that always carry identical values.
A true terminal state is task-defined and need not mean success; default FetchReach instead reaches its time-limit truncation without success termination.
terminated includes the external 50-step collection limit, while truncated is reserved only for numerical simulation failures.
At the external 50-step limit, the Q-learning target must discard its successor-value term because any stopped rollout is a true terminal task state.

stem: In the explicitly checked FetchReachDense-v4 setup (Gymnasium-Robotics 1.4.2), why is changing only ACTION_MAP’s fourth component insufficient to turn the reaching task into grasping?

options.text: Once the action table contains opening and closing values, actuator availability and the task reward no longer matter.
A fourth-channel command is sufficient because an effective actuator alone guarantees that a reaching reward will teach stable grasping.
Matching achieved_goal to desired_goal already certifies a stable grasp, even without an object-contact reward.
FetchReach ignores the gripper command and lacks a grasping objective; a suitable task, object interaction and effective gripper control are needed.

stem: With nonpositive returns, why can an untried zero-initialized action appear preferable to an action already updated to a negative Q value?

options.text: Zero is a measured return for the untried action because initialization is equivalent to one neutral experience.
Optimism guarantees that every state-action pair is visited sufficiently often, even when some states are never reached.
A negative update makes the sampled action permanently undesirable because later estimates cannot revise its ranking.
Zero can be optimistic relative to the learned negative estimate, so the untried action may win the greedy comparison.

stem: A registered environment is constructed with a supported rendering mode. Which trace correctly distinguishes construction, reset, stepping, rendering and plotting a saved reward history?

options.text: make constructs the instance; reset returns observation and info; step(action) advances the task; each render call then performs one additional physics step before displaying it; reward-history plotting is separate.

make constructs the instance; reset returns observation and info; step(action) advances the task; render plots the training loop’s saved reward history, so a separate Matplotlib history plot is unnecessary.

make constructs the instance; reset returns initial observation and info; step(action) advances the task and returns transition outputs; render visualizes the current task; plotting reward history is separate analysis.

make constructs the instance; reset returns only the initial observation; step(action) returns observation, reward, terminated, truncated and info; render displays the task; reward-history plotting is separate.

assumptions: The environment supports the explicitly configured rendering mode; exact render output type depends on that mode.
